items.title: 67250_John Collins oral history interview
items.q: I think Panama was on this -- Panama Francis, yeah... This was a unique, unusual record... Benny Carter was the leader... We had a bass player, Bob West... Jimmie Jones was playing piano.

ctx.x: You were saying earlier that someone who you recorded with wasn't stimulating musically. Who were some that you recorded with of the most stimulating people, musically, (inaudible).

Well, I was telling you about one recording I did with Ella Fitzgerald about -- I guess about two years ago. This was a unique, unusual record in that we did 30 tunes on one side, and we segued from one tune to another, never a break, just a direct segue. And it was a beautiful album. Benny Carter was the leader, and it was Georgie Auld, Edison Georgia All, Harry Sweets Addison, and Louie Bellson. We had a bass player, Bob West. Did I say Jimmie Jones was playing piano? Yeah, Jimmie Jones was playing piano. And I…
mind me about the last names because I --

That's right. But in New York, no. It's always something happening, and that I miss. And I hope one day to really I think that I may go back one day. Just -- but I go back once a year now just to listen and to see everybody and I saw Panama Francis there. You know, he was out here for a while, and he was doing very well but he just never got New York out of his system, so he finally said I've just got to go back, and he went back, and I saw him, he

had a big grin on his face, he was playing with Illinois Jacket. Jacques And this band, Illinois' band, was Hank Jones, Percy Heath, Panama, and Tiny Grimes. And it was just -- the band was popping, and Jacket when he saw me it was just beautiful. He ran over and hugged me and played his bassoon, I believe. This was his new instrument, he plays it very well.
